title: Change one user's retries, rewrite everyone's
topic: A spread that looks like a clone
blurb: The AI copied the default config with `{ ...obj }`. Then one override quietly edits the original.
prompt: This helper is supposed to give one request more retries without touching `DEFAULT_CONFIG`. The AI says the object spread makes a clean clone. Check it.
conclusion: AI summary: Spreading `DEFAULT_CONFIG` clones it, so `DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits.retries` stays at 2 no matter who calls `withRetries`. Safe for every request.

diagnosis_choices.label: Spread `{ ...obj }` is shallow, so `cfg.limits` still points to `DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits`.
`const` deeply freezes `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, so mutating `cfg.limits.retries` throws TypeError.
Object spread only copies primitive keys like `timeout` and skips nested objects like `limits`.
Declaring `const cfg` prevents line 4 from updating `cfg.limits.retries` in strict mode.

fix_choices.label: Clone the nested object too: `{ ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, limits: { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits } }`.
Replace `{ ...DEFAULT_CONFIG }` with `Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_CONFIG)` to copy nested keys.
Change `const cfg` to `let cfg` so the spread creates a mutable deep copy.
Call `Object.freeze(cfg)` on line 3 so `DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits` cannot be changed.

flaws.explanation: Spread (`{ ...DEFAULT_CONFIG }`) only copies top-level properties. `cfg.limits` and `DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits` point to the exact same object, so assigning `cfg.limits.retries` silently mutates the global default.
flaws.why_tempting: Using `{ ...obj }` is the standard idiom for avoiding mutation, and it works fine for flat objects like `timeout`.
flaws.catch_rule: Whenever you write `{ ...obj }` or `Object.assign`, check whether later lines mutate any nested object or array.
flaws.hint: Does `{ ...DEFAULT_CONFIG }` also make a new `limits` object, or does it keep pointing at the same one?

practice.problem: After `const a = { tags: ['x'] }; const b = { ...a }; b.tags.push('y');`, what is `a.tags`?
practice.answer: `['x', 'y']` — both objects still share the same `tags` array.

clean_conclusion: The outer config and the nested `limits` object are both newly allocated, so the default stays untouched.

diagnosis: `DEFAULT_CONFIG` is declared with `const`, which freezes `limits.retries` at `2` forever.
Putting `DEFAULT_CONFIG` outside `withRetries` makes it inaccessible inside the function.
Nested objects inside a `const` declaration cannot be spread in JavaScript.
Missing `Object.freeze(DEFAULT_CONFIG)` is fine — only `var` configs can be mutated.
fix: Change `const DEFAULT_CONFIG` to `let DEFAULT_CONFIG` so overrides work.
Pass `DEFAULT_CONFIG` as a second parameter to `withRetries`.
Flatten `DEFAULT_CONFIG` to `{ timeout: 3000, retries: 2 }`.
Move `DEFAULT_CONFIG` into a separate JSON file.

diagnosis: If `retries` is `0`, JavaScript treats it as falsy and keeps `2` instead of `0`.
Parameter `retries` collides with the nested property name `limits.retries`.
Missing default `retries = 2` throws ReferenceError when called with no args.
`withRetries` isn't marked `async`, so concurrent requests share `cfg`.
fix: Rename parameter `retries` to `maxRetries` so it doesn't shadow `limits.retries`.
Add a default `retries = 2` in the function signature.
Guard `if (!retries) return DEFAULT_CONFIG;` on line 2.
Mark the function `async` so each request gets its own stack.

diagnosis: Assigning `cfg.limits.retries = retries` throws TypeError because `cfg` was declared with `const`.
Dot notation `cfg.limits.retries` creates a new top-level key `'limits.retries'` instead of updating `limits`.
If `retries` is `0`, line 4 is a no-op and leaves `retries` at `2`.
Mutating `cfg.limits.retries` also overwrites `cfg.timeout` to `undefined`.
fix: Change `const cfg` to `let cfg` before line 4.
Use bracket notation `cfg['limits']['retries'] = retries;`.
Use `Object.defineProperty(cfg.limits, 'retries', { value: retries })`.
Reset `cfg.timeout = 3000;` right after line 4.

diagnosis: Returning `cfg` returns a reference to `DEFAULT_CONFIG` itself, not just `limits`.
Returning `cfg` strips nested objects like `limits` in strict mode.
Should return `cfg.limits` instead of the full `cfg` object.
Returning `cfg` without cloning lets the caller mutate `DEFAULT_CONFIG.timeout`.
fix: Return `{ ...cfg }` on line 5 so `DEFAULT_CONFIG` stays untouched.
Return `Object.freeze(cfg)` on line 5.
Return `cfg.limits` directly.
Return `JSON.stringify(cfg)` so callers can't mutate it.

diagnosis: Missing semicolon after `}` causes syntax errors in strict mode.
Leaving `withRetries` without resetting `DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits.retries = 2` causes the leak — just reset it here.
Nothing exports `withRetries` for other modules to call.
Closing brace leaves `cfg` allocated on the global object.
fix: Reset `DEFAULT_CONFIG.limits.retries = 2` before returning.
Add `};` at the end of the function.
Add `export default withRetries;`.
Set `cfg = null;` before closing.
